git_commit: dfd4400 (first run, INVALID for trail_ret_168h: name collision) / re-run after fix, committed with results
hypothesis: Long-horizon trend measures (trailing 7-day, 30-day, 90-day returns; distance of price from its 50-day and 200-day averages) carry DIRECTIONAL information about forward returns at the longer horizons (72h, 168h), consistent with the well-documented time-series momentum effect at monthly scales.
acceptance_criterion: PRE-REGISTERED before running. Direction: Spearman(feature, return_H) block-bootstrap 95% interval excludes zero with the same sign in BOTH exploration and validation. Magnitude: same, plus |rho| >= 0.10 both periods. Descriptive: mean 24h/168h forward return by 30-day trend regime.
feature_version: research features v1: trail_ret_168h, trail_ret_720h, trail_ret_2160h, dist_sma_1200, dist_sma_4800 (renamed from ret_* after the collision)

target.definition: signed forward return (direction) and absolute forward return (magnitude)
target.outcome: close of candle opening at as_of+H

point_in_time: trailing functions on a complete hourly grid; tests/test_features_point_in_time.py; dist_sma_4800 available only from ~2018-03 (34% of hours), dist_sma_1200 from ~2017-10
incident: FIRST RUN INVALID for one feature: the trailing 7-day return was named ret_168h, the same name the harness used for the forward 7-day return; the target overwrote the feature and 'correlated' 1.000 with itself (0.63 at 72h, 0.36 at 24h -- exactly the overlap between forward windows of different lengths). Caught by the 'too good to be true' rule. Fixes: feature family renamed trail_ret_*; harness targets renamed fwd_*; harness refuses reserved/colliding names; tripwire raises if any direction |rho| > 0.5; 3 regression tests (tests/test_feature_harness_guards.py). E001-E003 checked: no collisions there. Invalid output deleted; experiment re-run.

metrics.direction_pattern: exploration: trailing 30d/90d returns and dist_sma_1200 show weak POSITIVE momentum at 24-168h (rho 0.04-0.10, intervals exclude zero); validation: the SAME features are NEGATIVE (rho -0.01 to -0.11). Trailing 7d return: +0.02/-0.03. dist_sma_4800: +0.12/-0.11 at 168h.
metrics.magnitude_passes: none; trail_ret_2160h 1h consistent but 0.05-0.06 (below floor). dist_sma_4800 magnitude -0.17 exploration (far below the 200-day average -> bigger moves, i.e. bear markets are volatile) vs +0.05 validation.
metrics.decile_shape_24h: U-shaped |return| vs trailing return for every feature: big past moves either way -> big future moves. That is volatility clustering (E003) seen through a trend lens, not trend information.
metrics.regime_conditioning: exploration: mean 7-day return after 'uptrend' +3.1%, 'sideways' +0.4%, 'downtrend' -0.05% (momentum-like). validation: 'downtrend' +2.8%, 'uptrend' +2.6% (dips were bought in a bull market). Regime-dependent, not consistent.

results: NO long-horizon trend feature carries directional information that holds across both periods. The textbook monthly time-series momentum appears in 2019-2021 and vanishes or reverses in 2017-2018 and 2022-2025. The validation period (one long rise, 18 months) is short and one-sided, which limits what it can confirm -- but the exploration period alone, with 6+ years and two bear markets, also shows only weak and year-dependent effects. Magnitude: nothing beyond what E003's volatility measures already capture, and less consistent.
consistent_across_time: No. Sign flips between periods for every feature.
leakage_check: Post-fix: no feature name collides with targets (test); tripwire armed; point-in-time tests pass; the only strong correlations in the invalid run were the collision, which is now impossible.
overfitting_suspected: no -- nothing fitted. 25 direction tests, zero passes.
affected_design: No new feature adopted. The current 'trend' category's weakness (E002) is not fixed by looking further back. Together with E001-E003: price history alone has yielded one usable quantity (expected move SIZE from recent volatility) and no usable DIRECTION at any horizon from 1h to 7 days. Next groups (derivatives, macro) are genuinely different information and the honest place to look for direction.
notes: Roadmap note: if derivatives and macro also yield no direction, the project's deliverable becomes 'well-calibrated uncertainty + honest HOLD-heavy signals', which is a legitimate outcome under the brief.
